S No directions and  Registrar's order  with Signatures  15.07.2024 C482 No. 1816 of 2023  Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.

1. Ms. Lata Negi, learned counsel for the applicants, Mr. V.S. Pal, learned AGA along with Mr.
Sandeep Sharma, learned Brief Holder for the State and Mr. Amanjot Singh, learned counsel for the respondent/ complainant.

2. Pursuant to the previous order, the applicants as well as the respondent No. 2/complainant and Bhagirath Saini, the brother of the complainant, who is the husband of applicant No. 3 herein, are present in Court.
3. During pre-lunch sessions, this Court interacts with all of them and they all agreed to settle their dispute.

4. After post lunch sessions, a joint affidavit of applicant No. 3 and the brother of the complainant/respondent No. 2 Bharirath Saini is supplied to this Court, the advance copy of which was also supplied to the State counsel.
The said joint affidavit dated 15.07.2024 is also placed on record.

5. As per the joint affidavit, both the applicant No. 3 and her husband Bhagirath Saini have agreed to dissolve their marriage by way of mutual consent under Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act,
within four weeks from today.
6. In para 6 of the joint affidavit, there is reference of certain pending cases, and both the parties have agreed to withdraw all the pending proceedings.

Para 6 of the joint affidavit is being reproduced herein as below:-
"6. That both parties agree to withdraw all pending cases filed against each other in any court of law including case a. Case under section 125 case no. 497/2017 titled as Tejwati versus Bhagiath before principal judge family Court, Rampur b.

sentences.text: c. complaint case no. 1110/2017 titled as C482/1816/2023 on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11584866/

1 Tejwati versus Bhagirath and others before ACJM Rampur under section 498A, 354 IPC and 3/4 of DP Act.
d. complaint case no. 3278/2018 Bhagirath versus Nanhe under Section 323, 392,
427, 504, 506 of IPC, pending before Civil Judge (JD) Rampur."
7.

In para 8, it is also agreed that the husband (brother of the respondent/ complainant), who is also present in Court will pay a sum of Rs. 1,75,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Seventy Five Thousand Only)
towards permanent alimony, out of which Rs. 1,50,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Fifty Thousand Only)
have already been deposited with the Mediator Mr. Rijwan, resident of Ward No. 5, Mohalla Aglaga Swar Rampur, Uttar Pradesh.

8. The husband (brother of the respondent/complainant) and the complainant/ respondent No. 2 undertakes before this Court that the amount i.e. Rs. 1,50,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Fifty Thousand Only) which is lying with the Mediator will be handed over by tomorrow to the applicant No. 3 Smt.
Tejwati.
9. It is also agreed that remaining amount of Rs. 25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand Only) will be paid to her on the date of filing the application under Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act.

10. The applicant No. 2 herein is the real brother of the applicant No. 3 and he is also present in Court and this Court also interacted with him and he submits that he has no objection with the conditions as mentioned in the joint affidavit filed by the applicant No. 3 as well as by her husband.

11. List this matter on 02.09.2024.
12.

Mr. V.S. Pal, learned AGA for the State submits that since the brother of the respondent No. 2 settled the dispute with applicant No. 3 which is evident from the joint affidavit dated 15.07.2024,
he fairly submits that till the time both the parties fulfilled all the conditions of the joint affidavit,
the proceedings which is under challenge in the present C482 Application may be suspended.

13. After taking into consideration all these aspects, particularly, the fact that applicant No. 3 settled the dispute with her husband who is the brother of the respondent No. 2/complainant, further proceedings of Complaint Case No. 3830 of 2022, Rishi Saini Vs. Nanhey and others, pending in the Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Kashipur, District Udham Singh Nagar, shall remain stayed.
